title: Encrypted Access Audit Fabric and Compact Evidence Exporter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Deliver a production-grade 'audit fabric' that collects key-usage and encryption-policy events, compacts them into integrity-protected evidence bundles signed by the customer HSM or our KMS signing key, and publishes time-ordered bundles to our retention-backed export store for compliance attestations. This work focuses on the exporter side: compact bundle format, signing integration with HSM/KMS, residency metadata tagging, retention-aware lifecycle, and hooks for automated reporting generation.

Why this ticket exists:
- Current rotation and usage logs are verbose and scattered across services; auditors require compact, tamper-evident artifacts with verifiable signatures and residency windows.
- Existing evidence exports are manual and inconsistent across regions. We need deterministic bundles that map to rotation windows and retention policies for customers with strict residency requirements.

Success criteria / Acceptance tests:
1) Evidence bundle format v1 defined (JSON envelope + binary index) and documented in Confluence with examples.
2) Bundles are signed using either customer HSM-backed key (via KMS-HSM proxy) or Redwood signing key; signature verification runnable locally with provided verifier.
3) Export pipeline publishes bundles to region-tagged S3 buckets with lifecycle policy attached; export latency < 30m for completed rotation windows.
4) Retention labels are embedded and respected by downstream retention jobs (prune-on-retention-run).
5) Automated daily compliance report shows bundle counts, signature validity rate, and per-tenant residency compliance; surfaced in Console -> Compliance Dashboard.
6) Unit and integration tests + end-to-end demo with a tenant using VPC-private KMS.

High-level design:
- Event collector: lightweight job subscribes to key-usage and rotation events from audit-stream topic; normalizes events into canonical schema (timestamp, tenant_id, key_id, operation, region, residency_tag, rotation_epoch).
- Windowing & compaction: window events by rotation_epoch and time-slab; produce compact index (Merkle tree root for integrity) and optional protobuf-encoded payload for binary compression.
- Signing: call KMS-HSM-proxy service to request an HSM signature over the bundle root. Support for both customer-provided HSM keys (via tenant KEK path) and Redwood-managed signing keys. Signatures include signer_key_id, sig_algo, timestamp.
- Envelope metadata: residency_tag, rotation_epoch, earliest_event, latest_event, export_region, retention_policy_id, bundle_version.
- Exporter: atomic upload to region-specific export bucket with object metadata and server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). Buckets follow compliance retention lifecycle and are accessible only via audit-reader role.
- Verifier: small CLI/tool to fetch bundle, validate signature chain, verify Merkle proofs for sample events. This will live in tools/compliance-verifier repo (link below).

Trade-offs considered:
- Using Merkle trees vs simple digest lists: Merkle provides compact inclusion proofs for partial disclosure requested by auditors; cost added in CPU for building trees but better long-term usability.
- Synchronous signing vs queue-based async signing: chosen async (signing worker) to avoid impacting production path; ensures exporter can retry with exponential backoff.
- Bundle frequency: per-rotation_epoch + hourly slab vs per-hour only. We settled on rotation_epoch primary boundary with optional hourly shards to bound size.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: schema + Confluence spec, signer API contract, mock HSM adapter. (PR: draft in gh:redwood/compliance-evidence#214)
- Week 2: event collector + compactor prototype + unit tests. (PR: gh:redwood/platform-collector#872)
- Week 3: KMS-HSM-proxy integration + signer worker + integration tests with dev HSM emulator. (PR: gh:redwood/kms-proxy#56)
- Week 4: exporter to regional buckets, retention hook, verifier tool + demo. (PR: gh:redwood/compliance-exporter#101)

Operational considerations:
- Monitoring: metrics for bundle generation rate, signing latency, signature failures, export failures, and verification failure rate. Add Console dashboards and PagerDuty alerts when signature failure rate > 0.5% for 1h.
- Cost: compacting and binary encoding reduces storage; Merkle calculation increases CPU — added to runtime team budget.
- Security: all signing calls occur over mTLS; access to signing keys gated by tenant RBAC; HSM PKCS11 operations logged separately. Security review required prior to canary.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add an option for notarization (anchor Merkle root to public ledger) for high-compliance tenants? (requested by Legal).
- Retention enforcement: rely on S3 lifecycle + retention job, or add object-level TTL manifests? (ops preference: lifecycle + manifest).

Notes and links:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMPLIANCE/pages/CEV2-BUNDLE-SPEC
- Design sketch: GDrive: https://drive.google.com/example-bundle-design
- Dev HSM emulator repo: gh:redwood/hsm-emulator
- Draft PRs: gh:redwood/compliance-evidence#214, gh:redwood/platform-collector#872, gh:redwood/kms-proxy#56, gh:redwood/compliance-exporter#101

Why this is different from existing work: Unlike prior attestation tickets that focus on rotation proofing or long-term ledger anchoring, this ticket creates an operationally-friendly 'export fabric' that glues the event stream, compact integrity format, HSM signing, and retention lifecycle together with Console reporting. It prioritizes deterministic, verifiable bundles and an accessible verifier tool for auditors.
